hints.title: Core Idea
hints.text: We have 500,000 square feet of warehouse space. First prioritize packing the maximum possible number of prime items, then fill the remainder with non-prime items.

hints.title: Key Observation
hints.text: Compute the total square footage and item count for prime_eligible items, and determine how many complete sets can fit.

hints.title: Query Construction
hints.text: Use the remaining square footage to calculate how many complete sets of not_prime items can fit.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH T AS (
    SELECT
        IFNULL(SUM(square_footage), 0) AS s,
        COUNT(1) AS cnt
    FROM Inventory
    WHERE item_type = 'prime_eligible'
)
SELECT
    'prime_eligible' AS item_type,
    IF(s = 0, 0, cnt * FLOOR(500000 / s)) AS item_count
FROM T
UNION ALL
SELECT
    'not_prime',
    IFNULL(COUNT(1) * FLOOR(IF(s = 0, 500000, 500000 % s) / SUM(square_footage)), 0)
FROM Inventory
JOIN T
WHERE item_type = 'not_prime'
GROUP BY s
ORDER BY item_count DESC, item_type DESC;
```

complexity.notes: Aggregation of space requirements per category followed by greedy floor division.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Knapsack simulation is slow and unneeded since all items in a category must be replicated proportionally.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(1) memory for scalar space totals.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Compute prime capacity first and use remaining modulo space for secondary items.

solutions.approach: Capacity Floor Division with Modulo Remainder
solutions.code:
WITH T AS (
    SELECT
        COALESCE(SUM(square_footage), 0) AS s,
        COUNT(1) AS cnt
    FROM Inventory
    WHERE item_type = 'prime_eligible'
)
SELECT
    'prime_eligible'::varchar AS item_type,
    (CASE WHEN s = 0 THEN 0 ELSE cnt * FLOOR(500000 / s) END)::bigint AS item_count
FROM T
UNION ALL
SELECT
    'not_prime'::varchar,
    COALESCE(COUNT(1) * FLOOR((CASE WHEN s = 0 THEN 500000 ELSE (500000 % s::bigint) END) / SUM(square_footage)), 0)::bigint
FROM Inventory
CROSS JOIN T
WHERE item_type = 'not_prime'
GROUP BY s
ORDER BY item_count DESC, item_type DESC;
